title: Defence exports
definition: Value of defence goods and services exported from India, as reported by the Ministry of Defence. Counts authorisations realised, not order book.
notes: Nominal rupees, not inflation-adjusted. Roughly a third of the 2013-14 to 2025-26 growth is rupee inflation and depreciation.
FY2014-15 and FY2015-16 are omitted rather than estimated: no primary release was located for those two years at the time of verification.
The FY2018-19 spike and FY2019-20 fall largely reflect a small number of large contracts, not a trend reversal.

title: Defence production
definition: Total value of defence items produced in India by DPSUs, other PSUs and private firms in a fiscal year.
notes: FY2024-25 was first announced as ₹1,50,590 crore and later restated to ~₹1.54 lakh crore once remaining private-sector returns were counted. The revised figure is shown and flagged.
Production value counts output, not indigenous content. A platform assembled here from imported kits counts in full — this series is not a measure of self-reliance on its own.

points.note: First announced as ₹1,50,590 crore; restated to ~₹1.54 lakh crore.

title: Private sector share of defence production
definition: Share of total defence production value contributed by private firms rather than DPSUs and other public undertakings.
notes: Direction of 'good' is genuinely contested: a higher private share signals a broader industrial base, but says nothing about whether the output is indigenous or competitively priced.

title: Private sector share of defence exports
definition: Share of defence export value originating from private firms rather than DPSUs.
notes: Much of the private share is components and sub-assemblies feeding foreign primes, not finished platforms sold under an Indian badge.

title: Defence export authorisations issued
definition: Count of export authorisations issued by the Department of Defence Production in a fiscal year.
notes: An authorisation is a permission to export, not a completed sale. Counts breadth of exporter participation rather than value.

title: Ministry of Defence budget allocation
definition: Total Union Budget allocation to the Ministry of Defence, including defence pensions and civil expenditure.
notes: Includes pensions, which are roughly a fifth of the total and buy no new capability. Comparisons with China's or America's budgets that ignore this overstate India's usable defence spend.
Nominal rupees. Real growth after inflation is far shallower than the headline curve.

points.note: Implied by the 9.53% increase to FY2025-26.

title: Defence capital outlay
definition: Budget line for capital acquisition and infrastructure — the portion that buys new equipment rather than paying salaries and pensions.
notes: This is the single most informative defence budget line: it is what actually modernises the force.
Capital outlay has hovered near 26-27% of the defence budget for a decade. That ratio, not the headline total, is the constraint.
Capital outlay for FY2025-26 was reported as fully utilised at about ₹1.86 lakh crore against the ₹1.80 lakh crore budget estimate shown here.

points.note: BE; ₹1,48,723 cr acquisition + ₹31,277 cr R&D and infrastructure.

title: Estimated nuclear warhead inventory
definition: Independent expert estimate of India's total nuclear warhead stockpile as of January each year.
notes: India publishes nothing about its arsenal. Every figure here is an external estimate inferred from fissile-material production and delivery systems, with an error bar SIPRI itself describes as significant.
Treat this series as an order-of-magnitude indicator only. It is the least certain dataset on this site and is marked low confidence for that reason.

title: India's share of global major-arms imports
definition: India's share of world imports of major conventional weapons, measured by SIPRI trend-indicator value over rolling five-year windows.
notes: SIPRI's trend-indicator value measures military capability transferred, not money paid. It is not comparable to customs data.
A falling share is usually read as rising self-reliance. It can equally reflect delayed procurement — India's import decline coincided with well-documented acquisition delays.

points.note: Second largest importer, behind Ukraine at 8.8%.

title: Russia's share of India's arms imports
definition: Share of India's major-arms imports supplied by Russia, over rolling five-year windows.
notes: The halving of Russian dependence since 2010-14 is one of the clearest structural shifts in Indian defence procurement.
Legacy Russian platforms still dominate the in-service fleet; supplier diversification shows up in new orders long before it shows up in the order of battle.

title: Defence corridor investment committed
definition: Investment committed via MoU to each defence industrial corridor.
notes: Committed is not grounded. Against roughly ₹70,000 crore of commitments across both corridors, grounded investment is about ₹10,855 crore — around 15%.
Marked low confidence: figures come from ministry statements at differing dates with no single reconciled public register.

title: Defence corridor investment grounded
definition: Investment actually deployed on the ground in each defence industrial corridor.
notes: This is the number that matters, and the one rarely quoted. Grounded investment runs at roughly 15% of committed.
Marked low confidence: no independently audited register of grounded corridor investment was located.

title: Defence industrial corridors by status
definition: Count of announced defence industrial corridors by delivery status.
notes: Two corridors (UP, Tamil Nadu) are operating with land allotted and units producing. Two more (Maharashtra, Assam) are announced but not established.
Graded low confidence: the operational/announced split rests on ministry statements relayed by press, with no single reconciled public register.

title: Defence corridor nodes
definition: Count of designated nodal industrial locations within each established defence corridor.

points.note: Agra, Aligarh, Chitrakoot, Jhansi, Kanpur, Lucknow.

notes: Node lists are press-sourced. They are stable and uncontested, but no primary notification was located during verification, so this is graded low rather than treated as a record.

title: Direct jobs created in UP defence corridor
definition: Direct employment reported at units established in the Uttar Pradesh defence industrial corridor.
notes: Reported against a stated potential of 50,000 jobs — actual delivery is around a quarter of that.
No independent audit of these employment numbers was located.

title: MoUs signed in UP defence corridor
definition: Count of memoranda of understanding signed with the Uttar Pradesh defence industrial corridor authority, and land allotments made.
notes: 170 MoUs converted into 57 land allotments — a conversion rate of roughly one in three. Useful as a reality check on announcement-driven reporting.

title: Countries receiving Indian defence exports
definition: Approximate count of destination countries for Indian defence exports in a fiscal year.
notes: Reported as 'around 80 countries'. Breadth includes small consignments of parts and ammunition, so country count overstates strategic reach.
